scope.renderedRows: Non-platform catalog rows resolved through getComparisonClaim(). Generated repository metrics are governed separately by the freshness gate.
scope.platformHeaders: Products whose complete platform fact is Unknown are audited separately below. An omitted OS in a known platform list is not rendered as an Unknown table cell.
scope.parityRule: cells must exactly equal the current rendered non-platform Unknown keys. Implemented closures are recorded separately and are no longer Unknown catalog state.

cells.rationale: VibeTunnel forwards raw PTY input and is positioned for terminal agents, but its canonical repository does not define normalized approve/deny actions or exact agent follow-up semantics.
The repository documents deployment-dependent Tailscale WireGuard and ngrok TLS paths, not product-level end-to-end encryption across every VibeTunnel deployment.
VibeTunnel documents a responsive browser client and a work-in-progress native iOS app; no first-party native Android application is established.
Active/idle indicators are visible while using VibeTunnel, but the checked repository does not document push delivery or an out-of-app attention notification contract.
Shunt's product page describes installable daemon and clients but does not link a canonical public product-source repository, name a source license, or affirm that the shipped product is proprietary.
Shunt documents paired remote access without an exact end-to-end or zero-knowledge encryption claim for session content.
The checked Shunt page documents web/PWA and preview native iOS clients, not a native Android application.
The product page does not state whether remote traffic is direct, relayed by Shunt, or routed through a user-selected tunnel, so the security boundary cannot be assigned.
No supported vendor relay, direct-connect, or self-hosted relay deployment contract is identified on the checked exact-SKU page.
The page does not name TLS, SSH, WireGuard, application-layer encryption, or another exact transport-security mechanism for Shunt remote sessions.

The exact iPad guide recommends Safari/PWA and explicitly treats a third-party App Store wrapper as unsupported, so it does not establish a native code-server iOS client.
The canonical code-server material establishes a browser client but no first-party native Android application.
VS Code extensions can add agents, but the exact code-server sources do not provide a supported named coding-harness matrix and cannot inherit host-editor marketplace claims.
Editor UI notifications do not establish mobile push or an attention-notification contract for code-server itself.
Server workspace persistence and editor reconnection do not establish recorded terminal history or browsable coding-agent conversation history.

A persistent Code OSS workspace is not evidence of terminal recording or browsable agent conversation history.

implementedClosures.rationale: The exact Happy agent CLI exposes encrypted chronological message history per session, including bounded and JSON output.
Remote Control carries over the current conversation history and exposes named sessions through the claude.ai/code and mobile session list.
Remote Tunnels explicitly connects from VS Code desktop or a vscode.dev URL on a client of the operator's choosing.
The official tunnel workflow emits a vscode.dev browser URL and ships the Remote Tunnels extension in that web client.
sshx documents a hosted coordination relay while terminal content remains protected by client-side Argon2-derived AES end-to-end encryption.
Termix's optional AI Assistant proposes infrastructure changes for explicit user approval rather than applying them directly; this is narrower than arbitrary external-harness approvals.
Termix alert and automation rules can notify operators through ntfy, Discord, and webhooks, with firing and resolved history.

generatedMetricUnknowns.rationale: Repository metric Unknowns are generated collector failures or not-yet-refreshed values, not exact-SKU capability claims. The scheduled refresh and audit:freshness gate must close or block them; editorial research must not hand-fill those cells.
